subsystems.name: Electrolyzer stack
subsystems.role: splits water into hydrogen and oxygen using a proton-exchange membrane.

subsystems.name: Water management
subsystems.role: supplies and circulates purified water to the stack.

subsystems.name: Power supply and electronics
subsystems.role: provides DC power to the stack and controls the process.

subsystems.name: Gas processing
subsystems.role: separates hydrogen from oxygen and removes water vapour.

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: keeps the stack at an efficient operating temperature.

subsystems.name: Safety and control
subsystems.role: monitors pressure, temperature and hydrogen leaks.

buildSteps.title: Make the membrane electrode assemblies
buildSteps.detail: Catalyst (typically platinum and iridium) is coated onto a proton-conducting membrane, then sandwiched with gas diffusion layers.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the stack
buildSteps.detail: MEAs are stacked with bipolar plates and seals to form a series of cells, then clamped together to create a sealed unit.

buildSteps.title: Build the water loop
buildSteps.detail: Plumb in a reservoir, pump, deionizer and separators to feed pure water to the stack and recirculate it.

buildSteps.title: Add gas processing
buildSteps.detail: Install separators and a drying membrane to deliver dry hydrogen at the required pressure.

buildSteps.title: Integrate power electronics
buildSteps.detail: Connect a DC-DC converter, battery or solar input, and control electronics to drive the electrolysis.

buildSteps.title: Install safety systems
buildSteps.detail: Add pressure and leak sensors, and an automatic shut-off valve to stop hydrogen flow if a fault is detected.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Run with deionized water, check hydrogen purity and flow rate, and tune control parameters for stable operation.

buildSteps.title: Package the unit
buildSteps.detail: Mount everything in a rugged, portable case with ventilation and quick-connect fittings for water and hydrogen.
